summary: The desktop composer attaches any file, not only images. A non-image file (dropped, pasted or picked, up to 50 MB) is copied to <userData>/attachments/<uuid>/<name> and becomes a file chip above the editor; a dropped folder becomes a chip with its entry count and is not copied. On send each chip's token follows the typed text and expands to a line [Attached file "x" is saved at: /path] (or [Attached folder "x" is at: /path]), so every provider gets the path. A Claude turn also carries an attached PDF (20 MB and 100 pages at most) as a document block. A paste over 32 KiB becomes pasted-text-N.txt with a notice and a Keep inline action; Cmd+Shift+V pastes text inline. Chats on a remote machine take images only and name each refused file. Copies older than 30 days are removed at startup.

reactNativeIos.reason: No phone change. A sent attachment is a file pill in pills_meta (label such as spec.pdf (12 pages)) on a displayBody token, which the Expo thread already draws as a file chip. Attaching files from the phone is a separate feature.

nativeAndroid.reason: No phone change. Android shows a desktop file pill as the text it expands to, here the saved-path line, as it does for every other desktop file reference. Attaching files from the phone is a separate feature.

storageDataMigration.reason: Messages store the same displayBody and pills_meta shapes as before; an attachment is a file pill. Draft pills gain an optional attached flag in localStorage, which older builds ignore. The attachments folder is new and needs no migration.

updateRelease.reason: Desktop only, ships with the next desktop release. The headless server never registers the save channels, and the composer refuses files for chats on a remote machine.
